own_scenes.desc: La prensa juvenil (Boyfriend, Marilyn, Mirabelle, Fabulous, Honey, Rave, Nova) y la televisión difundían a toda velocidad modas e imágenes nuevas de feminidad. Cathy McGowan, copresentadora de Ready Steady Go!, era «la cara de los sesenta» y vestía de Barbara Hulanicki: con ella en pantalla cada semana, Biba se llenaba con cada nuevo modelo para chicas que tenían trabajo, comían poco y vivían en habitaciones de alquiler sin madre que las esperara. La androginia mod (pelo corto, ropa de chico) y la minifalda cambiaban el cuerpo. En febrero de 1966 Lesley Hornby, mod de Neasden de dieciséis años, salió de la peluquería de Mr Leonard con un corte de siete horas y el Daily Express la proclamó «THE FACE OF ’66»: Twiggy, la nueva chica de moda de un Swinging London que lo necesitaba, como si la fantasía de la «Kathy de diecisiete años» de Richard Mabey se hubiera hecho realidad.

influences.name: El pop en televisión: Ready Steady Go! y Top of the Pops

refs.q: ‘Cathy was the face of the 1960s,’ remembers Vicki Wickham.
refs.para: ‘Cathy was the face of the 1960s,’ remembers Vicki Wickham. ‘She was perfect, with the shiny straight hair and fringe, her clothes and fashion. She loved music too and was much more “mainstream” than I was. She was the perfect mod, and we had her on telly every week.’ Wickham and McGowan didn’t necessarily see what they were doing as political; they were just having fun. They were inspired by other women: not by Gloria Steinem or Betty Friedan, but by designers Barbara Hulanicki and Mary Quant.
refs.chapter: Mayo: Walkin’ My Cat Named Dog: la mística de la feminidad y la independencia femenina

refs.q: Biba had begun with an idea born out of rebellion.
refs.para: Biba had begun with an idea born out of rebellion. Hulanicki wanted to break the straitjacket of women’s clothing. Having been called ‘heavy boned’ by her mother, she wanted to make ‘skinny looking clothes’ for herself. ‘I wanted clothes cut with armholes so high up the body that your torso looked long and skinny.’ This fitted the needs and aspirations of her young clientele. ‘In the buoyant mid-sixties they all had jobs and were not used to eating massive meals.’
refs.chapter: Mayo: Walkin’ My Cat Named Dog: la mística de la feminidad y la independencia femenina

refs.q: ‘THIS IS THE FACE OF ’66’, proclaimed the headline
refs.para: ‘THIS IS THE FACE OF ’66’, proclaimed the headline, while McSharry described Twiggy as ‘the Cockney Kid with the face to launch a thousand shapes … THIS IS THE NAME, Twiggy (yes really) because she is branch slim, bends to every shape in fashion, and has her hair cut like a cap made of leaves. THIS IS THE LOOK that from this moment will launch thousands of clothes, a craze for freckles, dozens of hairpieces, and will cause a sell out in eye pencils.’
refs.chapter: Mayo: Walkin’ My Cat Named Dog: la mística de la feminidad y la independencia femenina
